9.1.crux: Animals reproduce in two ways: sexual reproduction needs two parents; asexual reproduction needs only one.

cards.title: Why reproduce?

steps.text: The adults produce young ones in turn, so the species continues

say: Reproduction makes sure that a kind of animal continues from one generation to the next.

cards.title: Two ways

cols.head: Sexual
cells: A male and a female gamete join

cols.head: Asexual
cells: One parent's body makes a new individual

say: Gametes are special reproductive cells: sperms from the male and eggs from the female.
cards.remember: Sexual = two parents; asexual = one parent.

cards.title: Same parents, similar young

items.text: A cow gives birth to a calf
A hen's egg hatches into a chick
A frog lays eggs that become frogs

say: Animals always produce young ones of their own kind.

crux_points: Sexual reproduction needs a male and a female parent and their gametes.
Asexual reproduction needs only one parent.

quiz.q: How many parents are needed in asexual reproduction?
quiz.why: In asexual reproduction a single parent produces the young one.

quiz.q: Male and female gametes join in…
quiz.why: Sexual reproduction involves the joining of a sperm and an egg.

9.2.crux: In sexual reproduction a sperm joins an egg (fertilisation) to form a zygote, which grows into an embryo and then a young animal, born either as a baby or from an egg.

cards.title: Reproductive organs

cols.head: Male
cells: A pair of testes, two sperm ducts, penis

cols.head: Female
cells: A pair of ovaries, oviducts, uterus

say: The ovary releases one mature egg into the oviduct every month.

cards.title: Female reproductive organs
say: This simple diagram shows the main parts as in your textbook.

cards.title: Male reproductive organs
say: Sperms are tiny single cells that can swim.

cards.title: Sperm and egg
say: When a sperm and an egg fuse, their nuclei join to form one cell: the zygote.
This is called fertilisation.

cards.title: Inside or outside the body
say: Frogs and fish lay hundreds of eggs in water, covered by a layer of jelly.
Many eggs and sperms are wasted, so they produce a lot of them.

cards.title: From zygote to baby

steps.text: It divides again and again into a ball of cells
Cells form tissues and organs: this is the embryo
The embryo grows in the uterus wall; when all body parts can be seen it is called a foetus

say: In a hen, a hard shell forms around the developing egg, and the chick hatches after about 3 weeks of warmth.

cards.title: Born or hatched?
say: 'Vivi' means alive and 'ovi' means egg.
cards.remember: Viviparous: born alive. Oviparous: hatch from eggs.

cards.title: Metamorphosis

steps.text: A frog lays eggs in water.
Eggs hatch into tadpoles (larvae) that look very different from frogs.
Tadpoles grow legs and lose their tails.

say: Such a big change from larva to adult is called metamorphosis.
Silkworms also go through metamorphosis: egg, larva, pupa, adult.

crux_points: Fertilisation is the joining of a sperm and an egg to form a zygote.
Fertilisation can be internal (humans, hens) or external (frogs, fish).
The zygote grows into an embryo; viviparous animals give birth, oviparous animals lay eggs.

quiz.q: What is marked '?' in this picture?
quiz.why: When a sperm and egg fuse, the single cell formed is the zygote.

options: Eggs and sperms meet outside the body, in water
quiz.why: Frogs release eggs and sperms into water, where they meet.

quiz.q: A hen is oviparous because it…
quiz.why: Oviparous animals lay eggs that hatch outside the body.

9.3.crux: In asexual reproduction one parent makes new individuals: Hydra grows buds, and Amoeba splits into two (binary fission).

cards.title: Budding in Hydra

labels.name: Young Hydra
labels.note: Bud separates and lives on its own

say: A small bulge called a bud grows on the side of the Hydra.
The bud grows tentacles, then breaks away to become a new Hydra.
cards.remember: Budding: a new individual grows out of the parent's body.

cards.title: Binary fission in Amoeba
say: First the nucleus splits into two, then the body divides.
'Binary' means two, and 'fission' means splitting.
cards.remember: Binary fission: one cell splits into two.

cards.title: Clones

steps.text: A clone is an exact copy of a living thing
Scientists in Scotland created Dolly the sheep in 1996
Dolly was the first mammal to be cloned

say: Cloning is an artificial way of making an exact copy.
Asexual reproduction in nature also makes young that are copies of the parent.

crux_points: Asexual reproduction needs only one parent.
Amoeba reproduces by binary fission: splitting into two.

quiz.q: What is marked '?' on the Hydra?
quiz.why: The bulge on the side is a bud that will become a new Hydra.

quiz.q: In binary fission, what divides first?
quiz.why: The nucleus splits first, then the rest of the body divides.
